Portal.modelsDescription: Compare performance, cost and speed. Choose a source and a ranking metric.
Portal.methodLivebench: LiveBench uses tasks with verifiable answers. Each category averages its subtasks; the overall score weights categories equally. Reasoning effort settings remain in model names.
Portal.methodCost: Cost per correct answer is a benchmark estimate in US dollars, not a subscription price. Benchmarks measure specific tasks: test candidates in your own workflow.
Portal.methodAA: Artificial Analysis provides intelligence, cost per task, speed, latency, total response time and context from its public table. Cost metrics depend on each source’s tests. Its indices use their own methodologies and are not combined with LiveBench scores. Public results retain the source’s rounding; a tie does not necessarily mean identical performance in the full data.
Portal.newsDescription: Releases, research and tools, straight from the sources.
Portal.newsNote: Automatically collected from sources without individual editorial review. Dates refer to the original publication. News covers the last 45 days and refreshes when the portal is visited.
Portal.experimentsDescription: Games, coding projects and model evaluations from the community.
Portal.experimentsNote: Automatic title search on Hacker News via Algolia, covering the last 30 days. Reports belong to their authors and have not been reproduced by Emada. Open the source and discussion to check methods, prompts and limitations.
Portal.voicesDescription: Posts from AI researchers, developers and leaders on X.
Portal.voicesNote: Posts about AI, models and tools, excluding replies and reposts. New posts are collected twice a day; busy periods may take more than one collection. Images, videos and full conversations remain in the original post. Dates and times are in UTC. Dated selections are identified.

livebench.overall: Equally weighted average of categories, on a scale from 0 to 100.
livebench.category: Average of available subtasks in this category, on a scale from 0 to 100.
livebench.cost: LiveBench estimate in US dollars per successful task: average cost per question divided by the overall score. Lower is better.

aaPublic.overall: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index as shown in the public table. Scores are rounded by the source; equal values appear tied.
aaPublic.costPerTask: Cost per task reported by Artificial Analysis, in US dollars. Lower is better. This differs from the price per million tokens.
aaPublic.speed: Median generation speed in the public table, in tokens per second. Higher is better.
aaPublic.latency: Time to the first response chunk, in seconds, from the source’s Latency First Chunk column. Lower is better.
aaPublic.responseTime: Total response time reported in the public table, in seconds. Lower is better.
aaPublic.context: Context capacity reported by the source, in tokens. The k and M suffixes are converted to thousands and millions; a larger context does not imply better quality.
aaPublic.note: Artificial Analysis public table, retaining the source’s precision and selection of models. * Indicates a source estimate. Missing values are excluded from the ranking. Refreshed every six hours when the portal is visited.

aaApi.overall: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. Compare only scores from the same source and version.
aaApi.coding: Artificial Analysis Coding Index, when provided by the API.
aaApi.math: Artificial Analysis Math Index, when provided by the API.
aaApi.speed: Median tokens generated per second. Higher is better.
aaApi.latency: Median time to the first token, in seconds. Lower is better.
aaApi.input: Price in US dollars per million input tokens.
aaApi.output: Price in US dollars per million output tokens.
aaApi.note: Data from the official Artificial Analysis API. Available metrics vary by model; missing values are preserved. Refreshed every six hours when the portal is visited.

Skills.title: Skills for working with AI
Skills.description: Find useful skills and reference repositories to expand your agent’s capabilities. Explore by task, meet the authors and check the sources.
Skills.introTitle: A good skill shows the way.
Skills.intro: Skills are packages of instructions, examples and resources that guide AI agents through specific tasks. Choose based on what you need to do: build an interface, review code, analyze data or prepare a document.
Skills.search: Search by skill, author or task…
Skills.skillCount: {count, plural, one {# skill found} other {# skills found}}
Skills.repoCount: {count, plural, one {# repository found} other {# repositories found}}
Skills.installHelp: With Node.js and npx available, run this in a terminal in your project folder and choose your agent. Check the requirements before use.
Skills.copyError: Could not copy. Select the command and copy it manually.
Skills.empty: No results with these filters. Try a different task or author.
Skills.criteria: This is an editorial selection, not a complete ranking. We considered Skills.sh installs, GitHub stars, identifiable authorship, documentation and usefulness for real tasks. We included popular collections and relevant official sources even when they have fewer stars.
Skills.metricsNote: Installs and stars indicate adoption and interest; they are not quality ratings or guarantees of results. Installs are approximate and stars belong to the whole repository. Numbers are a snapshot of the stated date and do not update in real time.
Skills.officialNote: “Official” identifies resources published by the organization behind the product, such as Anthropic, Vercel, OpenAI and Supabase. Collections group skills; directories link to resources by different authors; tools may need additional installation.
Skills.gettingStarted: How to choose and get started
Skills.stepOne: Start with a specific task. Read the SKILL.md and check whether its instructions match your goal.
Skills.stepTwo: Check the repository for agent compatibility, licensing and dependencies. Some skills need scripts, services, credentials or other skills.
Skills.stepThree: Use the skill’s command or the author’s recommended method. Try a small task and check the result before adopting it in your workflow.
Skills.homeDescription: Discover community instructions and workflows for design, code, documents and research.
